root_cause.text: In drm/vmwgfx, the vmw_translate_mob_ptr() and vmw_translate_guest_ptr() error paths were left using PTR_ERR(vmw_bo) after vmw_user_bo_lookup() was changed from returning a pointer to returning an int with an out-parameter, causing returns based on an uninitialized vmw_bo pointer instead of the actual lookup failure code.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both functions from `return PTR_ERR(vmw_bo);` to `return ret;` immediately after `ret = vmw_user_bo_lookup(..., &vmw_bo); if (ret != 0)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states the lookup API changed to “returned an error code with the pointer becoming an out parameter” while the code “continued to return the PTR_ERR of the now uninitialized pointer,” which could incorrectly report success and lead to uninitialized/OOB accesses.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes both functions from `return PTR_ERR(vmw_bo);` to `return ret;` immediately after `ret = vmw_user_bo_lookup(..., &vmw_bo); if (ret != 0)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states the lookup API changed to “returned an error code with the pointer becoming an out parameter” while the code “continued to return the PTR_ERR of the now uninitialized pointer,” which could incorrectly report success and lead to uninitialized/OOB accesses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return the actual vmw_user_bo_lookup() failure code in vmw_translate_mob_ptr() instead of using PTR_ERR() on vmw_bo.
intent_record.what: The error return in vmw_translate_mob_ptr() was changed from returning PTR_ERR(vmw_bo) to returning the existing ret value when vmw_user_bo_lookup(sw_context->filp, handle, &vmw_bo) fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now propagates the actual error code produced by vmw_user_bo_lookup() instead of deriving an error from vmw_bo, which may be invalid or unset on failure. This ensures correct error reporting and avoids returning an incorrect error value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return the real vmw_user_bo_lookup() failure code in vmw_translate_guest_ptr() instead of using PTR_ERR on vmw_bo.
intent_record.what: The error return in vmw_translate_guest_ptr() was changed from returning PTR_ERR(vmw_bo) to returning the existing ret variable when vmw_user_bo_lookup(sw_context->filp, handle, &vmw_bo) fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now propagates the actual error code returned by vmw_user_bo_lookup() instead of deriving an error from vmw_bo, which may not hold a valid error pointer on this failure path. This fixes incorrect error reporting and avoids returning an unrelated or invalid error value.

grouping_result.intent: Return the real vmw_user_bo_lookup() failure code in vmw_translate_guest_ptr() instead of using PTR_ERR on vmw_bo.

consistency_review.core_intent: Return the actual vmw_user_bo_lookup() error code from VMWare guest/MOB pointer translation helpers instead of incorrectly using PTR_ERR() on vmw_bo.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the described root cause by replacing erroneous PTR_ERR(vmw_bo) returns in vmw_translate_mob_ptr() and vmw_translate_guest_ptr() with the actual vmw_user_bo_lookup() error code after that function changed to return an int via out-parameter.

candidates.rationale: After vmw_user_bo_lookup() was changed to return an int error code via ret and use vmw_bo as an out-parameter, this statement incorrectly derives the return value from vmw_bo on the error path. Since vmw_bo may be uninitialized or not an ERR_PTR, this can return the wrong error code and embodies the root cause.

This identical error-path statement in vmw_translate_guest_ptr() uses PTR_ERR(vmw_bo) even though vmw_user_bo_lookup() now reports failure in ret rather than through an ERR_PTR return. That makes the function return an invalid value based on vmw_bo instead of the actual lookup failure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path return uses PTR_ERR(vmw_bo) after vmw_user_bo_lookup() was changed to return an int status and provide vmw_bo through an out-parameter. On lookup failure, vmw_bo may be uninitialized or not an ERR_PTR, so this statement returns an invalid error code instead of the actual failure code in ret. The same exact vulnerable statement appears in both vmw_translate_mob_ptr() and vmw_translate_guest_ptr().

Make the process of looking up a buffer object
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit b139d43dacef688a4f46f29eef34409e950f7cef
Author: Thomas Hellstrom <thellstrom@vmware.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 26 16:27:54 2018 +0200

    drm/vmwgfx: Make buffer object lookups reference-free during validation
    
    Make the process of looking up a buffer object and adding it to the
    validation list reference-free unless when it's actually added to the
    validation list where a single reference is taken.
    This saves two locked atomic operations per command stream buffer object
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable pattern described in the root cause is the post-API-change misuse of `vmw_user_bo_lookup()` where the code checks `ret` but then returns `PTR_ERR(vmw_bo)` on error, even though `vmw_bo` would not be a PTR_ERR-style return value and may be uninitialized. In this commit, that old pattern is not present in either affected function. Instead, `vmw_translate_mob_ptr()` now does `vmw_bo = vmw_user_bo_noref_lookup(sw_context->fp->tfile, handle);` followed by `if (IS_ERR(vmw_bo)) { ... return PTR_ERR(vmw_bo); }`, which is correct because the lookup function itself returns an ERR_PTR on failure. Likewise, `vmw_translate_guest_ptr()` uses the same correct pattern: `vmw_bo = vmw_user_bo_noref_lookup(...)` and `if (IS_ERR(vmw_bo)) ... return PTR_ERR(vmw_bo);`. The old `ret = vmw_user_bo_lookup(..., &vmw_bo, NULL); if (unlikely(ret != 0)) { ... }` logic has been removed from both functions. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent, and the function bodies already reflect the fix-compatible handling for the new lookup scheme.
